battlecards.why_selected: Matched 3.4% target fee, lowest total cost when credit-card fees unbundled, no transition disruption, strong functional fit.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year term (signed 4/15/2025); fee 3.4% of net collections; Year-3 increase capped at CPI+2%; credit-card processing fees paid directly by SaVida.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Full RFP with six bidders, benchmarks showing 3.4% market rate, executive escalation letter, growing collection volumes offered as commitment.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Integrated PM/RCM platform, existing workflows, responsive engineering support, scalable across sites.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Attempted above-market increase, potential 5% CPI clause in Year-3, limited behavioral-health specific analytics.
battlecards.switching_costs: Data migration, provider retraining, interface rebuilds—estimated 6-9 months and $250k+.
battlecards.key_contacts: Mercedes Dahar – Director of Customer Success
battlecards.notes: Plan to open re-negotiation in Year-2 to extend term and waive CPI uplift based on volume growth.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Initial price at 4% of collections above 3.4% target; implementation and data-migration risk; total cost of ownership higher than incumbent after transition costs.
battlecards.contract_terms: Round-1 proposal 4% of $32M collections (~$1.3M/yr); SaVida countered at 3.4%—no agreement reached.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Used as credible switch threat to drive incumbent pricing down.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Behavioral-health focus, flexible customization, positive peer references.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher pricing, limited in-house RCM services, unproven at SaVida scale.
battlecards.notes: Maintain relationship as future fallback option if Athena performance declines.
complexity_reasons: Provided competitive pricing used for leverage

battlecards.why_selected: Premier-tier pricing delivered 10–34% SKU reductions and enabled consolidation under one contract.
battlecards.contract_terms: Membership agreement signed 5/5/2025; evergreen with 60-day exit; pricing tied to Premier contract tiers; quarterly compliance reviews.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to shift total volume, competitive SKU benchmarks, commitment to full location roster.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad contract portfolio, immediate price drops, analytics dashboard.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Compliance requirements to keep tier pricing, indirect service via distributors.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low—membership can be cancelled; would need to re-negotiate pricing with individual distributors.
battlecards.notes: Next action: complete location enrollment and validate savings on Henry Schein purchases.

battlecards.why_selected: Offered unified managed-services solution with standard bandwidth and single consolidated invoice at reduced rate.
battlecards.contract_terms: Master services agreement under review (meeting 5/12/2025); expected 36-month term with rate lock and 99.9% SLA.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Consolidation of 30+ circuits, threat to move remaining sites to competing ISPs, bandwidth standardization.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Nationwide footprint, VPN/MPLS capability, dedicated account team.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Complex billing hierarchy, historical SLA issues at select sites.
battlecards.switching_costs: Early-termination fees on non-Comcast contracts; new circuit installation costs.
battlecards.notes: Ensure rollout schedule and SLA credits are embedded before signature.

summary.skipped_reason: Remaining suppliers were simple renewals, low spend, or lacked strategic negotiation details.
